'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****[[Operation Allies Refuge]]
*****[[The Pentagon|Pentagon]] spokesperson [[John Kirby (admiral)|John Kirby]] says that evacuations have resumed at [[Kabul]]'s [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/568127-evacuation-flights-resume-at-kabul-airport (''The Hill'')]
****[[Taliban]] member of the cultural commission Enamullah Samangani announces an [[amnesty]] across [[Afghanistan]] and urges women to join their government in the first mention of [[women's rights]] by the group since seizing Kabul: while Samangani did not specify what he meant by "amnesty", he said that "the [[Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan|Islamic Emirate]] doesn't want women to be victims" and that "they should be in the [[government of Afghanistan|government]] structure according to [[sharia law]]". [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/08/168e39f5c461-taliban-declare-amnesty-in-afghanistan-let-women-join-govt-report.html (Kyodo News)] [https://kstp.com/news/taliban-announces-amnesty-urges-women-to-join-government/6210038/ (KSTP-TV)]
****The Taliban says that they will respect women's rights and security under the Islamic Emirate, having encouraged women to return to work and allowed girls to return to school. [https://apnews.com/article/afghanistan-taliban-kabul-1d4b052ccef113adc8dc94f965ff23c7 (Associated Press)]
****Taliban spokesperson [[Zabihullah Mujahid]] says that the Taliban will hold their first news conference this afternoon in a media center in Kabul previously used by the former Afghan government. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/afghan-taliban-hold-first-news-conference-taliban-spokesperson-2021-08-17/ (Reuters)]
****[[National Security Advisor (United States)|U.S. National Security Advisor]] [[Jake Sullivan]] says that the Taliban is prepared to provide safe passage to civilians who are attempting to leave Kabul. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/08/17/taliban-pledged-safe-passage-of-civilians-to-kabul-airport-white-house-says.html (CNBC)]
****[[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Bob Menendez]] ([[Democratic Party (United States)|D]]-[[New Jersey|NJ]]) announces that the [[United States Senate Committee on Foreign Relations|U.S. Senate Committee]] will hold hearings into the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]]'s execution of the [[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|withdrawal]] of [[United States Armed Forces|American troops]] from [[Afghanistan]], as well as the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]'s [[Doha Agreement (2020)|deal]] with the Taliban. [https://www.axios.com/senate-democrats-investigate-us-afghanistan-troop-withdrawal-486c46fc-1213-4672-aeb5-bfaecf09531f.html (Axios)]
***[[Panjshir conflict]]
****[[Amrullah Saleh]], who served as [[Vice President of Afghanistan|First Vice President]] under former [[President of Afghanistan|president]] [[Ashraf Ghani]], claims on Twitter that he is now caretaker president, and that he refuses to surrender to the Taliban. Saleh is recorded travelling to [[Panjshir Province]] with [[Ahmad Massoud]], who has declared his opposition to the Taliban and also called for [[Panjshir resistance|anti-Taliban militia]] to assemble in Panjshir. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/-northern-alliance-flag-hoisted-in-panjshir-in-first-sign-of-resistance-against-taliban-101629215342032.html (''Hindustan Times'')] [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/1-afghan-vice-president-says-143754520.html (Yahoo! Finance)]
****Russian intelligence sources reported that Panjshir resistance forces loyal to [[Saleh|Amrullah Saleh]] had managed to re-capture [[Charikar]] and the surrounding areas of Parwan Province from the Taliban. [https://ria.ru/20210817/boi-1746127613.html (RIA Novosti)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*The eight people who went missing after their helicopter crashed into [[Kurile Lake]] in [[Kamchatka Krai]], [[Russia]], six days ago, are all found dead. Eight more people were on board but survived. [https://www.wral.com/all-8-dead-in-tourist-helicopter-crash-found-in-kamchatka/19828910/?version=amp (Wral)]
*A boat capsizes off the coast of [[Mauritania]] with 47 people on board presumed dead. The Mauritanian Coast Guard rescues several people from the sea. The boat had departed from [[Western Sahara]] and was travelling to the [[Canary Islands]], [[Spain]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/dozens-migrants-lost-sea-off-mauritanian-coast-2021-08-17/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 50,228 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 4,517,243. [https://en.mehrnews.com/news/177483/Iran-COVID-19-update-50-228-news-cases-625-deaths (Mehr News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] reports 8,716 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases since February 1. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/government-agrees-outline-for-students-in-grades-8-12-676897 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[Japan]]ese [[Government of Japan|government]] extends the existing [[state of emergency]] in [[Tokyo]], [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]], [[Okinawa Prefecture|Okinawa]], [[Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa]], [[Saitama Prefecture|Saitama]], and [[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba]], and also expands it to seven other [[Prefectures of Japan|prefecture]]s from August 20 to September 12. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/08/17/national/delta-surge-expanded-emergency/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 239 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 7,973. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2166551/record-239-covid-deaths-20-128-new-cases (''Bangkok Post'')]

***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Switzerland]]
****The number of fully vaccinated people in [[Switzerland]] surpasses 50%. [https://www.thelocal.ch/20210817/half-of-swiss-population-now-double-jabbed-against-covid (''The Local Switzerland'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency]] approves the usage of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] for children between the ages of 12 and 17, becoming the second [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] to be approved for use in children after the [[Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine]]. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-08-17/moderna-covid-vaccine-approved-for-12-to-17-year-olds-by-medicines-watchdog (ITV News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Cook Islands]]	
****The [[Cook Islands]] suspends its travel bubble with [[New Zealand]] and moves to Alert Level 2 following the confirmation of the first community case of COVID-19 in six months in New Zealand. [https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/travel/2021/08/cook-islands-closes-travel-bubble-with-new-zealand-after-covid-19-community-case-in-auckland.html (''Newshub'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]	
****[[New Zealand]] reports its first community transmission case of COVID-19 in six months in an unvaccinated 58-year-old man from [[Devonport, New Zealand|Devonport]] who tested positive after visiting a [[General practitioner|GP]] surgery and travelling to the [[Coromandel Peninsula]] during the past weekend. [https://i.stuff.co.nz/national/health/coronavirus/126097187/covid19-auckland-community-case-is-unvaccinated-man-58-who-travelled-to-coromandel (Stuff)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York City]]
*****[[New York City]] begins to implement mandatory proof of [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States|vaccination]] of at least one dose for people who want to dine in at restaurants or bars, watch public performances, or visit a museum or other cultural venue. However, the enforcement of these rules will not begin until September 13. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/n-y-c-begins-requiring-proof-vaccination-eateries-gyms-n1276991 (NBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Mexico]]
****[[Governor of New Mexico|New Mexico Governor]] [[Michelle Lujan Grisham]] announces that [[New Mexico|the state]] will reimplement its [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] and require vaccinations for high-risk settings. [https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/lujan-grisham-reinstitutes-mask-mandate-requires-vaccines-in-high-risk-settings/article_a733a86c-ff6e-11eb-9bf6-a748cabff4fc.html (''The Santa Fe New Mexican'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
****[[Governor of Texas|Texas Governor]] [[Greg Abbott]] tests positive for COVID-19. His office says that he is fully vaccinated and is not currently experiencing any symptoms. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/08/17/politics/texas-governor-greg-abbott-covid-19/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*Minister of Foreign Affairs of [[Peru]] [[Héctor Béjar]] resigns after a video of him claiming the [[Shining Path]] guerrilla group was propped up by the [[Central Intelligence Agency]] was published in local media. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-08-17/peru-s-foreign-affairs-minister-resigns-in-blow-to-castillo (Bloomberg)]
